e22_esb_population: The tail-silence-2s media variant of E22-ESB-TEST-UTTERANCES-2735: the SAME 2,735 published ESB test utterances of the six calibration-exposed calls that the sealed SAEA-E22-ESB-SHORTFORM-ALIGNMENT-V1 flight read once on 2026-09-05, re-encoded by one deterministic rule from the SEALED v1 WAV bytes by the model-free row SAEA-SN-MF-E22-TEST-TS2-MEDIA-V1. No draw, no sampling, no seed: this is the population, not an estimate of it. Per call: 4432298 351, 4450488 508, 4470290 178, 4479741 473, 4483338 619, 4485244 606. 24964.608437 s = 6.9346 h for one pass, 342563 audio tokens. Preregistration: docs/readiness/2026-09-07-e22-esb-shortform-tail2s-test-v1-preregistration.md.
e22_esb_variant_factor: the acoustic tail: exactly 2.0 s (32,000 zero samples) of digital silence appended to every clip, so the speech offset is followed by the clamp-floor mel features a stop produces instead of being followed immediately by the encoder's own unmasked zero-pad block. The 2026-09-07 encoding audit measured that appended digital silence lands on the clamp floor (median -0.7152 normalized) while the pad mtmd_audio_preprocessor_qwen3a inserts is the literal float 0.0, 0.72 units higher on a scale whose span is 2.0 and above 66.4 % of a clip's own real mel bins. On THIS population our path sends 17,695 audio tokens (6.52 % of 271,453) that the published HF path masks away, computed from 136,533 mel frames = 1,365.3 s of unmasked constant on 2,733 of 2,735 clips; per clip that masked-away share averages 11.53 % and reaches 76.92 % on the worst clip. The tail does not remove those tokens -- the same 17,695 are still sent -- it moves the block 2.0 s away: the pooled share falls to 5.17 % of 342,563 and the mean per-clip share falls to 6.74 % with the worst clip at 25.64 %.
e22_esb_identity_hash_convention: e22_esb_split_identity_hash is data.splits.split_identity_hash(prefixed('earnings22-original', sample_ids)) over earnings22-original/<call>-<segment>@ts2, the value core.flight.FlightRuntime.preflight computes at flight time and the value an exposure row must carry. It DIFFERS from the sealed test population's 9285b321... by construction: a variant clip never shares an identifier with its v1 twin, so no receipt, reference lookup or paired join can silently mix the two populations.
e22_esb_media_root: The 2,735 variant WAVs live under $SPEECHRL_DATA_DIR/derived/e22-esb-utterances/test2735-tail2s-v1 and never enter Git (798987810 bytes). They are deterministic transformations of the sealed v1 test bytes, each source file re-hashed against the committed D1 media supplement before it was read; no parent MP3 was opened and no decoder ran, so librosa never runs and the pinned absence of ffmpeg is preserved. The rule is the dev1500 builder's own transform, imported and pinned by sha256 49e5d910, so this population's bytes come from the same code as the dev1500 tail-silence-2s variant.
e22_esb_d1_media_supplement: The 2,735 @ts2 ids enter D1's identity closure through the additive media supplement named above (schema saea-d1-media-supplement-v1, the shape contracts.gate_media_identity reads); it chains to the same parent D1 identity artifact the v1 test supplement chains to, and binds to this population's own probe view through source_binding_sha256 aa5e677b.
e22_esb_split_role_basis: The 2026-09-04 owner decision re-designated the six ESB test calls calibration-exposed after one read; 109 confirmatory calls remain for final reporting and are not named, loaded, decoded or read here. contracts.plan.STAGE2_SPLIT_ROLES admits only 'discovery' and 'dev' and refuses 'confirmatory' outright, so 'dev' -- the role that means usable for calibration and never for final reporting -- is how calibration-exposed reaches the machine, exactly as the sealed test roster already expresses it. The successor receipt docs/receipts/splits-calibration-exposure-2026-09-04.json records the re-designation; docs/receipts/splits.json is NOT rewritten, its hashes are pinned. A SECOND READ of these six calls is what this population is for, and this fragment grants none: it needs the owner's explicit GO recorded in its own exposure row.
e22_esb_reference_boundary: The 'sentence' column is gold and NEVER enters the request path. The roster receipt this fragment names carries identifiers, media paths, measured media identity and segment spans only. References live in the SAME hash-pinned test reference layer the sealed 2026-09-04 flight was scored against, unedited, and the published segment key is recovered by splitting the sample id on '@' -- reproduction.esb_reference.published_segment_key performs that split, so a variant row scores against its own published sentence and against nothing else.
e22_esb_window_fit: The longest utterance is 4483338-281@ts2 at 38.360125 s. On the exact front-end rule the 2026-09-07 encoding audit derived and proved against 6,038 sealed prompt_tokens -- 13 tokens per 100 mel frames, n_eff = n_samples // 160 + 1 -- that is 507 speech tokens over five encoder windows. Worst required = 507 speech + the 49-token text envelope the sealed test smoke measured for this exact instruction + 1024 completion + 2 special = 1582, against the 4,096-token slot the sealed test flight's own -c 32768 -np 8 geometry gives: a margin of 2,514 tokens and a ratio of 2.59x on this repository's slot_tokens >= 2 x worst rule. FITS, so the sealed geometry is carried forward unchanged rather than re-derived.
e22_esb_exposure: This fragment grants no contact authority. docs/readiness/2026-09-07-e22-esb-shortform-tail2s-test-v1-preregistration.md, an owner GO and the exposure ledger do.
